chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of his companions, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman comes performing Tamattu', but she menstruates before she performs Tawaf by the House, and her purity comes to be on the Day of Arafaat.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she knows that she is pure to perform Tawaf by the House, and she could be free from her Ihram, and she could catch up with the people, then let her do so'.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهَا: Her state of Ihram (sacred ritual state)
key_terms.تَطُوفَ بِالْبَيْتِ: She performs Tawaf by the House (Kaaba)
key_terms.تَلْحَقُ بِالنَّاسِ: She catches up with the people (other pilgrims)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةً: Performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of pilgrimage combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she menstruates before completing Tawaf al-Ifadah during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for a woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah, emphasizing that her obligation is fulfilled if she purifies herself and completes the essential rites before the pilgrims depart from Mina. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the validity of the Hajj depends on the completion of core pillars rather than strict chronological adherence to the day of Arafat, provided the pilgrim rejoins the community in time. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate natural biological constraints without invalidating the pilgrimage.
